title: Blood
summary: Blood is the fluid the heart pumps. Strictly it is a connective tissue, but at this scale it behaves like a fluid organ: roughly 5 liters filling the vessels. A little more than half is plasma, a watery liquid carrying dissolved nutrients, hormones, and proteins. A little less than half is formed elements: red blood cells, white blood cells, and platelets. Blood carries oxygen and carbon dioxide, defends against infection, clots to seal leaks, and helps keep body temperature and pH steady.
connectsUp: Blood is what the cardiovascular system actually moves; the heart and vessels exist to keep it flowing.
deeper: The share of blood volume made up of red cells is the hematocrit, averaging about 45% and normally a little lower in females than in males. Blood is slightly alkaline, a little warmer than core body temperature, and several times more viscous than water, mostly because of its cells and plasma proteins.
clinical: Losing blood faster than the body can compensate causes hemorrhagic shock: with less volume in the loop, less oxygen reaches the tissues, however hard the heart pumps.

sources.title: OpenStax Anatomy & Physiology 2e, ch. 18.1: An Overview of Blood
